subject: Visibility, evidence, and exception path for SLOs at ACME
content:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.example>
To: Claire Adams <claire@acme-corp.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 04 Jan 2027 09:12 -0800
Subject: Visibility & evidence for SLOs — onboarding ask

Hi Claire,

Thanks for the time on Friday. Per your procurement checklist, I wanted to surface the concrete artifacts we can provide to ACME for SLO verification and ongoing visibility. High level summary below — I attached a short PDF with the same content.

What we measure (examples):
- Availability: minute-level success rate (2xx responses / total requests) computed per-customer at the API gateway.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 server-side generation time (ms) measured at the inference runtime, excludes customer network egress.
- Error rate: 4xx/5xx rates and internal service errors (retries/fails).
- Error budget: rolling 30-day window, availability target default 99.95% (customizable in Dedicated deployments).

Monitoring & alerting:
- We surface alerts on missed SLOs (thresholds configurable). Typical alerting for ops: p95 latency breach > 2x baseline sustained for 5m; availability drop > 0.1% in a 10m window.
- Alerts route to customer-run PagerDuty or our support on escalation; alerting history is retained in our observability backend and we can export incidents.

Customer access to metrics:
- Read-only Grafana role (observer) scoped to the ACME tenant. We can grant up to 5 named observers by default.
- Raw CSV exports for audit (per-request summaries, token-level histograms) delivered to a pre-authorized S3 bucket or via secure share.

Evidence we can hand over:
- 90-day rolling metrics export (CSV) and Grafana dashboard snapshot.
- Measurement documentation and formulae for each SLO.

Attachments: redwood-slo-metrics-overview.pdf (attached), grafana-invite.txt (contains invite link for read-only role).

Next steps? If procurement/security want a short walkthrough I can schedule a 30-minute session this week with our SE and security lead. Can you confirm the names/emails for the observers and procurement contact?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.example | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.example>
To: Claire Adams <claire@acme-corp.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.example, lauren_bishop@redwood.example, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 08:56 -0800
Subject: Re: Visibility & evidence for SLOs — onboarding ask

Claire — adding Priyom (Sales Engineering) and Lauren (Security) to provide the technical and compliance details. Below is a concise statement we can attach into your RFP. I also attached a CSV with the formulae.

Formal measurement statement (summary):
- Availability(sla): For tenant T, Availability_T = 1 - (failed_requests_T / total_requests_T) computed on a rolling 30d window, with per-minute aggregation. Failed requests include 5xx + internal retries that exceeded retry budget.
- Latency(sla): Latency_p95_T = 95th percentile of server-side generation latency for successful responses, measurement taken at the inference runtime just after the model output is produced and before network egress. Latency excludes client-side network time, and for cached responses we annotate the sample with cache_status (HIT/MISS) and compute separate percentiles.
- Error budget: ErrorBudgetRemaining = TargetAvailability - ObservedAvailability over the window; alerts when the burn rate sustains above configured thresholds.

How we deliver evidence:
- We can provide a signed CSV export containing per-minute aggregates for the last 90 days (attachment: slo-formula.csv).
- Grafana observer access for named SREs (link in grafana-invite.txt). Role is called 'tenant_observer_readonly'—no ability to modify dashboards or alerts.
- Audit logs for dashboard logins retained 13 months; queryable by time range and subject to NDAs.

Exception requests:
- For unusual measurement exceptions (e.g., planned migration where observed latency is not representative), customers submit an 'SLO Exception Request' form. The workflow is: submit request -> SE & CS review -> Product approval for temporary policy -> exec sign-off if request impacts availability targets or >72h window.
- We keep a numbered record (SLO-EX-####) and store decisions in HubSpot linked to the deal.

Attachments included: slo-formula.csv (per-SLO formulae), redwood-slo-metrics-overview.pdf (summary).

If this covers procurement's ask I can share the CSV & generate the Grafana invites once you confirm observer names.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example>
To: Claire Adams <claire@acme-corp.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.example>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 06 Jan 2027 14:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Visibility & evidence for SLOs — onboarding ask

Hi Claire, quick technical notes from the measurement side (happy to walk through offline):

- Tenant isolation: metrics are computed per tenant by tagging requests at the gateway. For Dedicated deployments we operate entirely within your VPC so metrics are still computed with the same runtime counters.
- Latency definition: We measure generation latency as time from request receipt at the runtime to the time the runtime finishes emitting tokens (server-side). Network egress and client queueing are excluded by default.
- Caching: cache hits are recorded as cache_status=HIT and we do not mix HIT and MISS samples in a single SLO; ACME can choose whether the SLO should include/exclude HITs.
- Outlier handling: we apply a z-score-based outlier filter on per-minute aggregates to reduce noise from noisy downstream systems; filter parameters are documented in measurement-readme.md (attached).
- Sampling: for extremely high QPS customers we compute exact percentiles via streaming t-digest and can also provide sampled raw distributions on request.

If you want, we can produce a sample export limited to request metadata (timestamp, latency_ms, status_code, cache_status) for the last 30/90/365 days. This is what procurement usually asks for.

-priyom
Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.example

Attachment: measurement-readme.md

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>
To: Claire Adams <claire@acme-corp.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.example>, priyom_das@redwood.example
Date: Sat, 09 Jan 2027 09:00 -0800
Subject: SLO exception path & access controls (formal)

Claire — quick note from security/compliance to make this formal for procurement:

- Dashboard role: 'tenant_observer_readonly' granted via our IAM; observers have read-only Grafana panels and cannot see or edit alerting rules. We will provision three named observer accounts for ACME by default; provide the full names + emails to ben and we will add them within one business day.
- Audit & retention: dashboard access logs and API query logs retained for 13 months; we can provide exported logs for your audit team.
- Exception workflow: SLO exception requests are submitted via our internal portal and generate an SLO-EX- record. Small exceptions (<72 hours of planned impact) are approved by Product + CS; anything longer or that modifies contracted availability requires Exec approval. Decision and rationale are stored with the exception record and shared as a PDF to your procurement contact.
- Escalation: our 24/7 on-call rotates across regional SEs. For ACME we recommend 1) page your SRE rotation, 2) page Redwood On-call (redwood-oncall@redwood.example) if you don't get a response in 15 minutes, 3) escalate to me (lauren_bishop@redwood.example) for org-level coordination.

We will also provide the SOC2 artifact subset referenced in your checklist via a secure S3 share once an MSA/NDA is executed.

If procurement wants the formal wording we can drop it into a short addendum for the MSA — Ben can coordinate.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.example
